source: store branches on github.com/mohamad-alakkad/genesis-lab + docs/reports (no synthetic values)

gen2-diagnosis.title: gen2 behavioral diagnosis
gen2-diagnosis.finding: gen2 learned efficient foraging (+53% seeds vs the scripted survivor) but not hiding: 0.3% of threatened time in shelter vs 22% for the survivor; caught in 70% of episodes vs 47%. Held-out survival plateaued after ~14M steps.
gen2-diagnosis.cause_hypothesis: Discovery problem, not a reward bug: meadows were placed >= 2.2 u from any shelter edge in a 24x16 world, so the payoff of hiding is delayed and rarely experienced.
gen2-diagnosis.change: World v2.1.0 (meadows 2-4 u from a shelter edge; stalking audible at 2.5 u) and a fresh lineage gen3 from random weights. No reward for hiding was added.

gen3-diagnosis.title: gen3 failure decomposition and strategy ceilings
gen3-diagnosis.finding: Perception is sufficient (no capture without warning; median 5 s warning). gen3 flees in the open (52% dash) and runs through shelters (64% dash inside) instead of hiding; it leaves shelter while still sensing the predator (73%). Reactive hiding is nearly worthless here (oracle 645 ticks); preemptive avoidance works (oracle 1069). With Vela's own senses, survival rises monotonically with cue memory (724 → 933 ticks).
gen3-diagnosis.cause_hypothesis: The winning strategy needs memory of recent predator percepts and a horizon long enough to value staying hidden (gamma 0.99 ≈ 10 s).
gen3-diagnosis.change: gen4: 2×2 controlled experiment on world 2.2.0 (memory inputs on/masked × gamma 0.99/0.997), 2 seeds per cell.

gen4-results.experiment: gen4 2x2: memory inputs (on/masked) x gamma (0.99/0.997), world 2.2.0, paired init seeds 1-2
gen4-results.evaluation: held-out family 'standard', 200 episodes per checkpoint, fresh seeds 3e9+50000..50199 (disjoint from the seeds used to select 'best'; same for all arms), deterministic argmax, run's own input mask
verdict: gamma 99: memory 739.3 vs masked 634.6475 ticks → memory better (CIs separated)
gamma 997: memory 1059.2 vs masked 1074.1825 ticks → no CI-separated memory effect
mem: gamma .997 1059.2 vs .99 739.3 ticks → longer horizon better (CIs separated)
nomem: gamma .997 1074.1825 vs .99 634.6475 ticks → longer horizon better (CIs separated)

interpretation.horizon: Dominant cause. gamma 0.997 vs 0.99: +320 to +440 survival ticks, CI-separated with and without memory; capture 64–71% → 36–38%. The gen2/gen3 plateau was mainly short-horizon credit assignment (≈10 s), which made greedy foraging look optimal.
interpretation.memory: Helps only with the short horizon (+105 ticks at gamma 0.99, CI-separated); no effect at gamma 0.997 (1059 vs 1074, CIs overlap). Not the main cause.
interpretation.strategy_learned: Trace of gen4-mem-g997-s1 best (28.0M), 60 held-out episodes: evasive flight that breaks line of sight. When the predator is sensed 47% of actions are dash (9% otherwise); enters a shelter in 27% of threat bouts (gen3 12.5%) but leaves while threatened in 72%; median predator distance 7.0 u; 20 captures in 60 episodes (gen3 47); median warning before a capture 74 ticks. Sheltered-under-threat stays low (3.5%): it did NOT learn to sit hidden.
interpretation.vs_references: Best gamma-0.997 arms (≈1060–1070 ticks) exceed the scripted survivor (724) and the memory-150 sensory hider (933) and match the privileged oracle's survival (1069), but the oracle is caught far less (17% vs ≈36%).
interpretation.deployed: gen4-mem-g997-s1 best (28.0M): lowest capture on fresh seeds (29%).
